literal: Giving without letting the destitute speak the distress of saying 'I have nothing' exists only with one who has noble lineage.
translation: Giving to the needy even before they have to utter the painful words, 'I have nothing,' is a virtue found only in those of noble birth.
modern: 'எனக்கு ஒன்றும் இல்லை' என்று இரப்பவர் தன் துன்பத்தைச் சொல்லும் முன்பே அவருக்குக் கொடுக்கும் குணம், நற்குடியில் பிறந்தவரிடமே இருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the highest form of charity. True giving does not wait for a needy person to undergo the painful humiliation of begging and uttering the words 'I have nothing' (இலன் என்னும் எவ்வம்). A person of noble character and lineage (குலனுடையான்) senses the distress of others and gives generously before they even have to ask (உரையாமை ஈதல்). This proactive generosity is described as a rare quality that exists only with those of noble birth.
